The Manager, International Customer Supply Chain will play a key role in delivering an exceptional customer and retail partner experience across rhode’s growing international business.

This role will partner closely with Sales, Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Finance, Operations, international distributors and retail partners to ensure strong execution across order management, inventory flow, launch planning, and ongoing customer supply chain performance.

This role will support multiple international markets and distribution partners, requiring strong coordination across regions and global supply chain processes.
This is a highly cross-functional role that requires strong analytical skills, clear communication, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where processes are still being built. The ideal candidate is proactive, solutions-oriented, and comfortable moving between day-to-day execution and longer-term process improvement.
A core focus of this role will be building strong relationships with key retail partners, understanding their supply chain requirements, supporting innovation and promotional planning, identifying and mitigating supply risks, and using customer data to improve in-stocks, fulfillment, and overall service levels.
\n

Serve as a key point of contact between rhode and international distributors and retail customer operations teams, supporting day-to-day execution and market-specific supply chain needs
Continually assess opportunities to improve customer supply chain, reduce operational costs, and drive volume through supply chain metrics
Develop a deep understanding of each international distributor and retail partner’s distribution model, operational requirements, key metrics, and inventory planning needs
Strong analytical skills to produce qualitative/quantitative data (using Excel, PowerPoint, NetSuite, Tableau) that can be shared to drive business
Broad understanding of policies, processes and systems relating to retail distributor operations
Overseeing and ensuring smooth order processing and timely delivery across international customers, distributors, and retail partners with focus on Innovation planning and customer expansion
Provide weekly sell in data vs. forecast and any risks associated to the month/quarter plan to Finance, Sales and Operations stakeholders
Track & monitor weekly sell out data coupled with retailer in stock levels in partnership with Demand planning and Sales account leads
As needed, partner with international distributors, retailer Supply Chain & planning teams to drive additional orders or forecast adjustments guaranteeing appropriate inventory coverage
Track and report on key international customer supply chain KPIs, including fulfillment, in-stocks, service levels, on-time delivery, and potential chargeback risk
Internal and external collaboration for alignment and identifying opportunities
Participate and contribute to customer demand forecasting, maximizing forecast accuracy
Participate and influence assortment decisions aimed at optimizing sales and productivity by utilizing analytics, market research, consumer research, and customer intelligence
Partner closely with international teams, distributors, and cross-functional stakeholders to support new market launches, regional assortment expansion, and ongoing operational excellence.
Ability to connect internal functions to drive supply chain improvements (fill rate, on-time, in-stocks, reduce potential chargebacks, customer program execution) for the customer
Help educate and align internal teams on international customer expectations, distributor requirements, regional retailer requirements, and best practices for execution

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain or another analytical field preferred or equivalent experience
5+ years of experience in customer supply chain, retail operations, customer logistics, demand planning, supply planning, or related operational roles
Must have experience with Sephora and/or other global prestige beauty retailers
Experience supporting international retailers, distributors, or global customer supply chain operations.
Strong communication skills both verbal and written
Excellent Excel Skills and knowledge
Proven ability to build strong relationships with retail partners, internal cross-functional teams and deliver results
Ability to make thoughtful decisions when data is limited, ambiguous, or evolving
Experience managing multiple countries, distributors, or regional supply chain requirements
Willingness to travel internationally is required
Other Details for Consideration
Location of Position: United Kingdom and European Union
Travel Expectation: Must be willing to travel internationally for the business and to our HQ when needed

Das erwartet Dich bei uns: Du möchtest praktische Erfahrungen im Supply Chain Management sammeln und dabei aktiv zum Erfolg eines internationalen Unternehmens beitragen? Dann werde Teil unseres Teams!
Bei uns erhältst Du spannende Einblicke in die Bereiche Bestandsmanagement, Bedarfsplanung und Logistik. Gemeinsam mit erfahrenen Kolleg:innen arbeitest Du an Projekten, analysierst Prozesse und unterstützt dabei, unsere Lieferkette noch effizienter zu gestalten.
Verstärke unser Team zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt als Werkstudent Supply Chain Management (m/w/d) !
Deine Aufgaben: Vielfältige Einblicke: Du unterstützt unser Supply-Chain-Team in den Bereichen Bestandsmanagement, Bedarfsplanung und Logistik.
Analysen & Auswertungen: Du erstellst Auswertungen, analysierst Kennzahlen und leitest gemeinsam mit dem Team Optimierungspotenziale ab.
Projekte begleiten: Du wirkst bei spannenden Optimierungsprojekten mit, beispielsweise zur Verbesserung der Warenverfügbarkeit und Lagerbestände.
Prozesse verbessern: Du unterstützt bei der Definition, Dokumentation und Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen entlang der Supply Chain.
Schnittstellenmanagement: Du arbeitest eng mit den Bereichen Customer Service, After Sales, Finance und weiteren internen Teams zusammen.
Logistik koordinieren: Du stehst im Austausch mit externen Logistikdienstleistern und unterstützt bei operativen Fragestellungen.
Praxisnah lernen: Du erhältst tiefgehende Einblicke in das Tagesgeschäft einer internationalen Supply-Chain-Abteilung und lernst unser ERP-System SAP kennen.
Was uns überzeugt: Dein Studium: Du absolvierst aktuell ein wirtschaftswissenschaftliches, logistikbezogenes oder technisches Studium.
Deine Zahlenaffinität: Du hast Freude am Umgang mit Daten, Analysen und Auswertungen.
Deine Systemkenntnisse: Du verfügst über gute MS-Office-Kenntnisse, insbesondere in Excel.
Deine Arbeitsweise: Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und lösungsorientiert.
Dein Mindset: Du bist neugierig, lernbereit und bringst Dich gerne mit eigenen Ideen ein.
Deine Kommunikationsstärke: Du arbeitest gerne mit verschiedenen Teams zusammen und fühlst Dich auch im internationalen Umfeld wohl.
Deine Sprachkenntnisse: Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse runden Dein Profil ab.

Über tonies: tonies ist die weltweit führende interaktive Audioplattform für Kinder mit mehr als 10 Millionen verkauften Tonieboxen und 125 Millionen verkauften Tonies.

Das intuitive und preisgekrönte Audiosystem hat mit seinem kindersicheren, kabellosen und bildschirmfreien Ansatz die Art und Weise verändert, wie junge Kinder selbstständig spielen und lernen. Tonieboxen wurden bereits in über 100 Ländern aktiviert, und das Content-Portfolio umfasst rund 1.400 Tonies in mehreren Sprachen.

Seit der Gründung hat tonies bedeutende Meilensteine erreicht, darunter den Börsengang an der Frankfurter Wertpapierbörse im November 2021 sowie den Aufbau eines weltweit präsenten Teams von über 550 engagierten Fachkräften, die in verschiedenen Ländern tätig sind.
Teil unseres tonies-Teams zu werden bedeutet, an einer inspirierenden Mission teilzuhaben: innovative und bedeutungsvolle Erlebnisse für Kinder auf der ganzen Welt zu schaffen. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft des Spielens, Lernens und der Fantasie.
Du als Teil von tonies: Bei tonies bist du nicht einfach nur eine „studentische Hilfskraft“ – du bist ein voll integriertes Teammitglied. Du erhältst tiefe Einblicke in die Supply Chain einer schnell wachsenden, globalen Marke und bekommst die Möglichkeit selbst echte Verantwortung zu übernehmen.
Während andere vielleicht von wachsenden To-Do-Listen überwältigt werden, behältst du einen kühlen Kopf und konzentrierst dich auf das Wesentliche. Du blühst auf, wenn es darum geht, komplexe Probleme in einem globalen, dynamischen Umfeld zu lösen, das durch flache Hierarchien und agile Entscheidungsfindung geprägt ist.
Deine Aufgaben umfassen: Operative Unterstützung: Unterstützung des Global Supply Planning-Teams bei der Nachverfolgung internationaler Lieferungen von unseren Lieferanten zu den lokalen Lagern, Gewährleistung einer termingerechten und präzisen Durchführung von ERP-Transaktionen, Überwachung von Lagerbeständen sowie die Analyse und Optimierung von Kernprozessen der Lieferkette.
Datenmanagement: Unterstützung bei der Zusammenstellung und Aufbereitung kritischer Datensätze, die als Grundlage für präzise Bedarfs-, Liefer- und Bestandsprognosen dienen.
Systeme & Administration: Pflege und Optimierung unseres ERP-Systems sowie Abwicklung allgemeiner kaufmännischer Aktivitäten innerhalb der Lieferplanung und des operativen Einkaufs.
Reporting & Analytics: Erstellung umfassender Berichte, Verknüpfung verschiedener Datensätze sowie Unterstützung bei der Nachverfolgung von KPIs und der Prozessdokumentation.
Abteilungsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit: Unterstützung des Teams an den Schnittstellen zu anderen Abteilungen, um einen reibungslosen Ablauf der Supply-Chain-Aktivitäten zu gewährleisten.
Was wir uns von dir wünschen: Ausbildung/Studium: Du bist derzeit in einem Studiengang der Betriebswirtschaftslehre (BWL), des Supply Chain Managements, der Logistik, des Wirtschaftsingenieurwesens oder eines verwandten Bereichs immatrikuliert.
Berufliche Fähigkeiten: Erste Erfahrungen durch Praktika oder Werkstudententätigkeiten in einem Unternehmensumfeld sind von Vorteil.
Kommunikation: Fließende Kommunikationsfähigkeiten sowohl in Deutsch (C1) als auch in Englisch (B2) sind erforderlich. Ein sicheres Auftreten und eine kooperative, teamorientierte Denkweise runden dein Profil ab.
Analytische Denkweise: Es macht dir Spaß, komplexe Informationen logisch zu strukturieren und klar zu präsentieren. Du arbeitest mit hoher Präzision und Gewissenhaftigkeit.
IT-Kenntnisse: Du bist ein fortgeschrittener Anwender von MS Office (insbesondere Excel) und bringst eine natürliche Neugier für das Erlernen neuer IT-Umgebungen und ERP-Systeme mit.
Selbstmanagement: Du bist ein proaktiver Selbststarter mit exzellentem Zeitmanagement und der Fähigkeit, dich schnell an neue Anforderungen anzupassen.
Warum tonies? Globales Teamwork: Wir arbeiten über Abteilungs- und Ländergrenzen hinweg an unserer Vision, die Toniebox in jedes Kinderzimmer der Welt zu bringen.
Come as you are: Das gilt nicht nur für den Dresscode, sondern auch für alles andere. Denn nur dort, wo man sich wirklich wohlfühlt, kann man sein Bestes geben.
Erholung & Freizeit: Genieße 20 Tage bezahlten Jahresurlaub (basierend auf einer 5-Tage-Woche) sowie drei zusätzliche freie Tage (Rosenmontag, Heiligabend und Silvester).
Sprachenlernen & Entspannung: Verbessere deine Kommunikationsfähigkeiten mit der Sprachlern-App Babbel und finde Entspannung durch unseren Zugang zur Meditations-App Calm.
Rabatte: Profitiere von attraktiven Rabatten auf unser gesamtes tonies-Produktsortiment.
Gut zu wissen: Als Teil unserer Grundsätze setzen wir uns aktiv für Inklusion und Vielfalt bei tonies ein. Wir schätzen und feiern die unterschiedlichen Fähigkeiten, ethnischen Zugehörigkeiten, Glaubensrichtungen und Geschlechter unserer Kolleginnen und Kollegen. Jede*r ist herzlich willkommen und wird in jeder Phase der gemeinsamen Reise in seiner/ihrer Entwicklung unterstützt.
Wir freuen uns darauf, von dir zu hören!

JOIN OUR TEAM As a Senior Supply Chain Manager , you will own and continuously improve the end-to-end flow of goods across our supply chain network. You will act as a senior partner to cross-functional teams, including buying and warehouse operations, to ensure the timely delivery of products to our customers.

Furthermore, you will work with suppliers, driving supply chain resilience to meet purchase order management requirements and ensure product availability. As the central expert for supply chain operations, you will play a key role in shaping best practices and mentoring team members. This position is permanent and based in Munich .
WHAT YOU'LL DO Own the end-to-end purchase order lifecycle, from supplier onboarding and order placement to shipment management and tracking, ensuring product availability across a complex, multi-category portfolio
Coordinate deliveries, resolve shipping issues, and partner with freight providers, warehouse operations, buying, and supply planning teams to ensure efficient order fulfillment and smooth logistics operations
Monitor and evaluate KPIs (e.g., OTIF, OTP, product availability), conduct root cause analyses, and implement structural improvement plans
Lead cross-functional projects to improve supply chain processes, resolve systemic bottlenecks, and drive a culture of continuous improvement through best practices, operational excellence, and innovative solutions by utilising AI and automation where applicable, while ensuring compliance with company policies and industry regulations
Build and lead strategic, long-term relationships with key suppliers, acting as the senior point of contact and driving supplier performance and smooth purchase order execution
Lead, coach, and develop a team of two direct reports
YOU COME WITH A bachelor's degree in supply chain management, logistics, or a related field
5+ years of experience in supply chain management, preferably in a similar role
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and supply chain management software; experience with data analysis tools (e.g. Excel, SQL, Tableau) is a plus
Ability to work independently and thrive in a team-oriented environment, as well as excellent communication and interpersonal skills, enabling effective collaboration with diverse stakeholders
Fluency in English

Duties may include, but are not limited to: Oversees and manages strategic planning, auditing, quality assurance, and program compliance and oversight of all SCM programs and inspections as well as various activities designed to enhance the mission of the affected VISN and its facilities.

Identifies all activities involved supporting the needs of supply chain, including capital asset planning, lifecycle management of equipment, strategic sourcing of commodities such as clinical supplies, maintenance supplies and services, subsistence, medical gases, and durable medical equipment and services for inpatient and inpatient services home care.

Establishes, oversees, monitors, and manages the performance and measurement of Supply Chain support functions throughout the VISN. Conducts Supply Chain audits, compliance reviews, and program effectiveness/efficiency reviews based on self- developed and nationally developed standards of all VISN facilities.

The NPI Prototype Procurement Manager owns fast-turn prototype sourcing during new product development. When engineering needs a part quoted and built in days, not weeks, this role makes it happen, and makes sure the part we source for a prototype build doesn't quietly become a bad default for production.
This role reports to the Director of Supply Chain and works closely with engineering, our prototype contract manufacturers, and our production sourcing team. Prototype CMs are good at turning parts fast; they are not set up to decide which of those parts should become a real production supplier, or to catch when a rushed sourcing decision is costing us on markup or quality risk down the line. That decision needs a dedicated owner on our side.
We are building this role now because the gap is already showing up in real costs: parts moving slower than they should, and markups on prototype-CM-sourced parts that we're paying today without anyone tracking whether that's the right long-term call.
Scope
Fast-turn sourcing: for parts that are strategic, long-lead, or clearly headed toward production, you run the RFQ and sourcing decision directly rather than letting a prototype CM default-source it under time pressure.
Prototype-to-production tracking: for parts a prototype CM sources on our behalf, you track what was bought, from whom, and at what cost, and you flag early which of those should transition to a qualified production supplier instead of carrying forward by default.
Cost visibility: you own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging anything trending over target early enough to actually do something about it.
This role sits specifically in the handoff between early prototype builds and production. Production commodity strategy, supplier negotiation, and cost-out on qualified production parts stay with our sourcing team. Day-to-day material tracking and expediting once a part is in production stays with our materials team. This role owns the messy middle: prototype-stage sourcing decisions that determine what production inherits.
This role starts as an individual contributor working in close partnership with engineering.
Who this role is for
You have direct experience sourcing prototype and early-production parts in a hardware environment, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering while designs are still moving. You're comfortable quoting and placing an order on a part that might change again next week.
You think past the next build. When a prototype shop sources a part fast, you're the person asking whether that supplier, that price, and that quality level are good enough to carry into production, or whether it needs to change before it's too late to change cheaply.
You're comfortable working through and around a contract manufacturer's own sourcing team rather than owning a factory floor yourself. You know how to get a CM's buyer to move fast for you, and you know when to route around them and source directly.
You have a cost-conscious streak. You notice when a markup looks high and you're willing to do the work to find out if it's justified.
You are comfortable in early-stage environments where the playbook is still being written, and where this specific handoff between prototype and production sourcing hasn't had a dedicated owner before.
This role is not a fit for
You are looking to own production commodity strategy or long-term supplier negotiation. That sits with our sourcing team.
You are looking to own day-to-day material tracking and expediting once parts are in production. That sits with our materials team.
You need stable designs and a locked BOM to work effectively. This role lives in the period before that’s true.
You would find a startup operating tempo frustrating.

Prototype sourcing
Run quick-turn RFQs and place orders directly for strategic, long-lead, or clearly production-bound parts during prototype builds.
Partner with engineering embedded in design reviews and build planning, understanding what’s changing and what’s stabilizing.
Manage supplier relationships for quick-turn shops separate from our production supplier base.
Prototype-to-production handoff
Track every part sourced by a prototype CM on our behalf: supplier, cost, and whether it’s fit to carry forward.
Flag parts that should transition to a qualified production supplier early enough to make the change before it’s expensive.
Hand off qualified parts and supplier context cleanly to our production sourcing team, with a clear paper trail rather than tribal knowledge.
Cost visibility
Own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging cost overruns early.
Identify where prototype CM markups are worth the convenience and where a direct sourcing decision would save real money.
Cross-functional partnership
Partner with our production sourcing team on the handoff for parts moving from prototype to production.
Partner with our materials team on build timing and part availability during prototype phases.
Partner with engineering on design-for-sourcing input while parts are still changeable.

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably.

We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products.

From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

We're looking for a Senior Inventory Planner to own product launch planning and post-launch replenishment execution for Quince's UK and EU expansion. This is not a steady-state replen role. It's the planner who decides how deep we go on new products at launch, then operates the day-to-day to make sure those products actually land on time and scale well.
You'll size initial launch buys for products dropping into the UK and EU at a weekly cadence, often with little or no local demand history, by triangulating from Quince overall performance, comparable products, comparable markets, lead-time realities, and informed judgement.

Once products are live, you'll act on early sell-through signals and trigger replenishment decisions fast, pulling forward, doubling down on winners, cutting losses on losers, and adjusting the next launch wave based on what the market is teaching us.
This role sits at the heart of Quince's International expansion. Working alongside a planning and automation counterpart who owns the underlying forecasting models and demand sensing, you'll be the operator who turns those signals into real-world action.

Sizing the buys, placing the POs, working the relationships, and getting product in the warehouse on time. Your edge is judgement, speed, and the trust you build with the people who make execution actually happen.

You'll be operating where the tooling is still being built around you, the data is thinner than you'd like, and the answer often has to be reasoned from first principles. Comfort operating in a dynamic environment isn't a nice-to-have, it's the job.
The ideal candidate has lived this work before. Sizing launch buys, executing replenishment decisions, working POs through to landing at a DTC or M2C that moves quickly and has international exposure. You're a builder of relationships first and a builder of spreadsheets second.

You're energized by placing well-reasoned bets under uncertainty, by getting product to land on time when it shouldn't have, and by the trust you accumulate with vendors and cross-functional partners over time. You communicate constraints bluntly but constructively.

You don't wait for perfect data, and you don't let a winning product sit understocked while you wait for statistical significance.
Success in This Role Means
Product launch buys are sized well. Products that are market winners aren't crippled by stockouts and losers don't tie up working capital you can't recover.
Post-launch product replenishment decisions are fast and well judged. Safety stock and WOS is controlled and refreshed as market signals mature. Winning products scale into demand, losing products get cut before they bleed.
Forecast accuracy improves measurably on new products, even where historical data is thin.
POs land on time, in full, and any deviation is known, flagged, and managed proactively
Merch, sourcing, production partners, vendors, and your peer planners in other geographies trust you completely. You're the person they pick up the phone for, the one whose word on a PO they take to the bank, the one they share early intelligence with.
Inventory turns improve as the UK and EU business scales
The launch and replen frameworks you build for the UK don't just serve the UK today. They become the blueprint for how Quince plans every new market launch that comes next.

Own end-to-end launch planning for new products entering the UK and EU markets. Size the initial buy, sequence against lead times and launch dates, and translate it into clean PO recommendations
Take forecasting models, demand signals, and algorithmic recommendations developed by the team and operationalize them. Apply judgement on top, raise issues when the model is wrong, and feed real-world execution learnings back to improve the models
Manage POs end-to-end. Generate, adjust, expedite, and follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure on-time, in-full delivery against launch dates
Partner closely with merchandising on assortment and launch calendars, and with sourcing and production on lead times, capacity, vendor allocation, and PO execution. These are your primary day-to-day partners
Build and nurture strong working relationships with partners directly. Communicate constraints clearly, hold them accountable to commitments, escalate constructively when needed, and become the partner they prioritize when capacity is tight
Work as part of a global planning community. Share intelligence with planning counterparts in the US and other geographies, lift and adapt their analogs and learnings into UK and EU plans, and escalate cross-market issues quickly
Build and maintain the operational artifacts (trackers, dashboards, status notes) that give the rest of the business confidence in launch readiness and post-launch performance
